subject: Monthly availability buffer & credit escrow proposal
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Finova Contracts <contracts@finova.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template — monthly buffer + escrow for credits

Hi Rachel / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed the draft SLA and they raised one operational ask we want to get your thoughts on: instead of Redwood applying monthly invoice credits after the fact, Finova would prefer a short-term escrow mechanism for credits tied to availability bands. The idea is to: 1) pre-fund a small monthly buffer into an escrow account, 2) if availability falls below the agreed threshold for the billing month, credits are released from escrow to offset that invoice, 3) if no credits are triggered for three consecutive months, escrow balance rolls back to Redwood.

Specific asks from our side:
- Baseline uptime: 99.95% for hosted (Finova will accept dedicated contract if you require higher SLA).
- Credit bands: define % credits per monthly band and a clear cap (procurement prefers a cap at 100% of that month’s hosting fees).
- Escrow administrator: we prefer a neutral third party (DocuSign escrow or our procurement bank).
- Turnaround: claims need to be processed within 10 business days of incident close.

Can Redwood operate under an escrow hold for equivalent credits, or do you prefer invoice adjustments? If escrow is feasible, we’ll have our legal attach a short term-sheet.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can move to redlines.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Manager — Finova
[Attachment: procurement-sla-notes.docx]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template — monthly buffer + escrow for credits

Elena — thanks for outlining this. Good to hear procurement’s perspective. Quick responses inline below.

On Mon, 12 Jul 2026 at 08:15, Elena Park wrote:
> Baseline uptime: 99.95% for hosted (Finova will accept dedicated contract if you require higher SLA).

We typically publish 99.95% for Hosted API in the standard template; Dedicated/Private customers often request 99.99% and we treat that as a committed target on Dedicated. So 99.95% is within our standard Hosted profile.

> Credit bands: define % credits per monthly band and a clear cap (procurement prefers a cap at 100% of that month’s hosting fees).

We can propose a clear banding table. Our typical hosted credit schedule is: 99.95% and above — no credit; 99.5–99.949% — 10% credit; 99.0–99.499% — 25% credit; below 99.0% — 50% credit, with an overall cap of 100% for the billing period. If you’d like a different mapping, we’re open to adjusting band widths.

> Escrow administrator: we prefer a neutral third party (DocuSign escrow or our procurement bank).

Operationally we can support a ‘credit bank’ model where Redwood holds accrued credits on the account (preferred for operational simplicity). That said, we are open to escrow arrangements for large enterprise deals if Finova requires independent administration. There are some practical items to confirm: who funds the escrow (usually Redwood would seed a small holding for the first 1–3 months during a transition), fees for the escrow provider, and how we reconcile partial-month incidents.

> Turnaround: claims need to be processed within 10 business days of incident close.

We can commit to triaging SLA claims within 10 business days; settlement (i.e., credit application or escrow release) will typically follow contract terms but we’ll aim for 15 business days for settlement once investigation is closed.

I’ve attached a short term-sheet and a redlineable SLA-draft (SLA-draft-v3.pdf) that includes a proposed credit bank workflow and an optional escrow clause. Ben — can you confirm if finance is okay with the seed/holding approach for escrow on enterprise deals?

Next steps:
- Finova legal to send redlines on the attached SLA draft.
- If escrow is required, send the proposed administrator and fee schedule.
- We can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk the term-sheet.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-draft-v3.pdf (pdf, 145KB)]

From: Contracts <contracts@finova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Finova legal redline request (escrow detail)

Begin forwarded message:

From: "Connor Mills" <connor.mills@finova-legal.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
To: Contracts <contracts@finova.com>
Subject: Redlines: escrow clause & cap

Rachel / Marissa,

We reviewed SLA-draft-v3 and attached redlines to the escrow section. Key items: 1) explicit monthly cap of 100% of that month’s Redwood hosting charges (no offsetting other invoices without express consent); 2) escrow administrator must sign a simple release form triggered by the signed minutes from technical incident review; 3) any maintenance windows >4 hours to be notified 14 days in advance to avoid escrow triggers.

We’re sending the redline PDF now. Please confirm you’ll accept the 14-day notification and the 10-business-day claim window; procurement will not agree to longer settlement timelines.

-Connor

[Attachment: finova-redlines-sla-escrow.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>, Contracts <contracts@finova.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Finova legal redline request (escrow detail)

Looping in quick commercial position so legal has context. Short answers:
- Baseline: Hosted = 99.95% (OK). For reference, Dedicated would be 99.99%.
- Credit banding: I’m okay with the proposed band schedule Rachel outlined above; we should explicitly call out a monthly cap at 100% and an annual reconciliation clause so neither side builds up unreasonable liability.
- Escrow: Redwood pricing/ops team prefers a credit bank operated by us (simpler). If Finova insists on third-party escrow, Redwood will agree for enterprise deals but will ask for a small one-time setup fee to cover third-party escrow administrative costs and a short seed balance during onboarding (we can absorb the seed for this pilot).
- Turnaround: 10 business days triage + 15 business days settlement is acceptable to us as long as Finova provides timely post-incident approvals.

Proposed next step: Rachel — can we offer a 30-minute call on Wed 14th at 10am PT to walk the redlines and the escrow checklist? I’ll bring finance to confirm the seed/fee details.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Commercial Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@finova.com>, Contracts <contracts@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly availability buffer & credit escrow proposal — next steps

Elena / Connor / Contracts team — thanks for the redlines and the clear requests. Confirming the action items we agreed internally and on the call: 

1) Redwood accepts baseline 99.95% hosted SLA and will include the credit band table in the next redline.
2) Redwood accepts a monthly cap of 100% of that month’s hosting fees per Finova request.
3) Escrow: Redwood prefers to operate a credit bank, but will accept third-party escrow for this enterprise deal. Redwood will absorb the onboarding seed for the trial period and will invoice a one-time escrow admin fee if Finova chooses a third-party administrator.
4) Turnaround: Redwood will triage claims within 10 business days and aim to settle/release credits within 15 business days of incident-close and approval.
5) Maintenance notification: Redwood agrees to provide a 14-day notice for maintenance windows expected to exceed 4 hours; standard scheduled maintenances under 4 hours will follow our published maintenance window policy.

Next steps:
- Finova legal to send finalized redlines on SLA-draft-v3.pdf (we received finova-redlines-sla-escrow.pdf).
- Redwood legal will prepare a clean counter with an optional escrow addendum and the credit bank workflow included.
- Schedule: proposed call tomorrow (Thu 15 Jul) 10:00am PT / 13:00 ET to finalize terms.

I’ve attached the term-sheet with the optional escrow language and a simple credit-escrow term sheet for finance to review (credit-escrow-term-sheet.xlsx). If you’d like Redwood to propose two escrow vendors we can send that list this afternoon.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: credit-escrow-term-sheet.xlsx]
